card.hook: Picture an old heritage train, green hills behind it, and a café tucked inside a vintage carriage. Freshwater Station is the friendliest place to start your Kuranda Scenic Railway photos.
card.stand_here: Stand on the platform at Freshwater Station, roughly beside the carriages where the train leaves for Kuranda. Face the train so the carriages run across your screen with the hills behind.
card.zoom: Use zoom 1x to fit the carriages and station buildings together. If the platform is narrow and you can't get the whole train in, tap 0.5x. Try 2x (if your phone has it) for the locomotive and small details.
card.make_it_pop: Turn on your gridlines and line the carriages up along one of the horizontal lines so the train looks straight.
card.best_time: Pick a departure time and shoot the platform scene before you board. If you want Barron Falls, they flow strongest after rain, so January to February beats the drier months. Only some services stop at Barron Falls Station, so check your timetable.
card.selfie_here: At Kuranda Railway Station, stand on the platform with the parked train behind you while it waits to return to Cairns. Use the front camera, try 0.5x, and the carriages, which are decorated with Aboriginal artwork, make a colourful backdrop for a close-up.
card.ask_someone: At Kuranda Railway Station, stand on the forecourt by the heritage building (down the stairs from the Skyrail cableway station) and ask a passer-by to stand back from the platform so the train fits in.
card.rules_and_safety: Photography is permitted and encouraged on the train, including at the Barron Falls photo stop. Skip the flash inside the carriages if it might disturb other passengers. At Barron Falls, stay on the platform and behind the barriers.
card.challenge: Get one wide shot of the whole train, then hunt down the best close-up: a carriage door, a station sign or the locomotive. Which one wins?
card.good_to_know: Work on the line began in 1886, and passenger services started on 25 June 1891. Builders cut 15 hand-made tunnels and built 37 bridges to lift the track from sea level to 328 metres. The line is 37 km long, and a one-way trip takes about one hour and 55 minutes.
card.stand_here_before_gps_rule: Stand on the platform at Freshwater Station, roughly beside the carriages where the train leaves for Kuranda. Face the train so the carriages run across your screen with the hills behind.

card.hook: Here's a nice bit of luck: still water, palms, fish sculptures and the Cairns skyline all line up in one frame. Not many spots do that without you hunting for it.
card.stand_here: Stand in Fogarty Park, about 210 m north-west of the lagoon, and face north-west. The lagoon and waterfront sit in front of the city skyline from here.
card.zoom: Start at zoom 1x for the lagoon against the skyline. Go to 0.5x for more water and sky, or 2x (if your phone has it) to pick out the buildings behind.
card.make_it_pop: Keep your phone level and switch on the gridlines so the waterline stays nice and straight.
card.best_time: Some people love the lagoon at high tide, others prefer sunrise along the boardwalk. If you're staying nearby, take a few frames at different times and pick your favourite. Check tide times if you want high water.
card.selfie_here: Stand in front of the Torres Strait woven fish sculptures at the lagoon's edge with the pool behind you. Use the front camera, and try 0.5x to squeeze in more of the water. At high tide, the deep-water edge of the main pool's beach section gets an infinity-pool look behind you.
card.rules_and_safety: Drones are typically restricted near the lagoon, so check local rules if you travel with one. Lifeguards are on duty during the lagoon's opening hours, and it's worth checking those hours before you go.
card.challenge: Get a palm or a fish sculpture in the foreground of your skyline shot, then see if it suddenly looks twice as big.
card.good_to_know: The lagoon sits on Cairns' waterfront, with the sea beyond it and the town behind. For the classic close-up, walk down to the water's edge afterwards, where the ocean sits behind the water and the fish sculptures and palms frame the scene. Coconut Grove, the palm-lined walkway along the Esplanade, is good for framing sky and sea instead.
card.stand_here_before_gps_rule: Stand in Fogarty Park, about 210 m north-west of the lagoon, and face north-west. The lagoon and waterfront sit in front of the city skyline from here.

selfie_spots.why: A guide calls the fish-shaped water features Insta gold, and they sit at the lagoon's edge, so they can frame a selfie with the pool behind.

selfie_spots.why: One guide says a high tide turns the pool's edge into an infinity-pool look, which works well for a selfie with the water behind you.

The 'infinity edge' spot depends on high tide, and sources give different lagoon opening hours, so check before going. No page I found mentions selfie-stick or tripod rules.

card.hook: Picture a long row of shed roofs marching along the water, with a clock tower poking up behind them like it's keeping an eye on the boats. That's the old working side of Cairns, and it looks great on a phone.
card.stand_here: Stand on Wharf Street, on the stretch running down to the complex's number 2 gate, and look east. The sheds and gateway sit in the middle of your frame, with the city streets leading down to Trinity Inlet.
card.zoom: Start at zoom 1x for the sheds and gateway just as you see them. Go to 0.5x to fit in the whole roofline or get close to the gate, and try 2x or 5x (depending on your phone) for the clock tower from further away.
card.make_it_pop: Switch on the gridlines, line the street up with the middle of the frame so the sheds sit evenly on each side, and keep your phone level so the long roofs don't lean.
card.best_time: Early morning or late afternoon are kinder than harsh midday sun in Cairns. In the afternoon, looking east, the sun is behind you and lights up the front of the sheds.
card.selfie_here: Try the north end of the wharf, with the rustic wooden groins behind you. Use the front camera, and zoom 0.5x if you want more of the scene in. One 2018 blog also rates this end for photos in front of the yachts, but it may have changed, so check what's in your frame when you get there.
card.rules_and_safety: Wharf Street is a public street, but the wharf area and cruise terminal may have restricted access at times, so check the official site before you go.
card.challenge: Take three shots of the same view, one close, one from the middle of the street and one from further back, and see which one makes the clock tower look best.
card.good_to_know: The complex was built in stages between 1910 and 1948 and added to the Queensland Heritage Register on 17 December 1999. Concrete wharves with long sheds on top replaced the old timber jetties, and Cairns was the first Queensland port to use reinforced concrete wharves to any real extent. The clock tower was added above the number 3 shed in 1948, and that shed is now the Cairns Cruise Liner Terminal.
card.stand_here_before_gps_rule: Stand on Wharf Street, on the stretch running down to the complex's number 2 gate, and look east. The sheds and gateway sit in the middle of your frame, with the city streets leading down to Trinity Inlet.

selfie_spots.name: Cairns Wharf, north end of the wharf
selfie_spots.detail: at the north end of the wharf, with the rustic wooden groins of the wharf behind you
selfie_spots.why: A 2018 Cairns travel blog says the wharf's wooden groins make a good backdrop for outfit photos, and it recommends the north end of the wharf for photos in front of the yachts.

sources.title: The Most Instagrammable Places In Cairns (The Daily Luxe)

selfie_research.notes: Only one selfie spot was found. The main source is a 2018 blog post, so the advice may be dated. The blog describes the wooden groins as a background for outfit photos, but it does not clearly say the wharf complex itself is in frame at the north end, so check on arrival. No page I found names a spot where a passer-by should stand to photograph a visitor with the whole Cairns Wharf Complex, so ask_someone_spot is null. No page I found mentions selfie stick or tripod rules or a safety point for this site.

card.hook: A shark glides slowly towards you, and in your photo it's mostly a reflection of your own face. Cairns Aquarium has the big, slow animals and steady blue water that make a good picture, but the glass fights back.
card.stand_here: Stand at the Cairns Aquarium itself, where the phone icon on the map sits. Once you're inside, get right up close to the glass of the big tanks and face the water.
card.zoom: Use zoom 1x for most tank shots. Switch to 0.5x in front of the biggest tanks to fit the whole scene in. If you can't get close to the glass, try zoom 2x to 5x (depending on your phone) for a single fish or ray.
card.make_it_pop: Tap the animal, then slide the brightness down a little so the water stays a rich blue instead of going grey.
card.best_time: The tank lighting is the same all day, so the time hardly matters indoors. Pick a quieter moment if you can, because it's easier to get a clear spot at the glass. For a shot of the building from outside, daylight is easiest.
card.selfie_here: Try the footpath in front of the main entrance on Florence Street, at the corner of Abbott Street. Use the front camera with the entrance behind you, and try 0.5x if your phone has it to squeeze more building in. This is a best guess, so check it when you arrive.
card.ask_someone: Ask a passer-by to stand on the footpath across Florence Street, directly opposite the Ramada by Wyndham, while you pose in front of the entrance, so the whole front of the building fits in the frame.
card.rules_and_safety: Flash photography isn't allowed, to protect the animals. Selfie sticks (photo extension poles) may not be used to cross into the exhibits.
card.challenge: Turn on the gridlines and wait for a shark or ray to swim your way. Put it on a line with empty blue water in front of its nose, and no chasing allowed.
card.good_to_know: Cairns Aquarium opened in 2017. It has three levels, 71 tanks and more than 15,000 animals in 10 habitats. The Billabong Amphitheatre is Australia's largest freshwater tank at 400,000 litres. Some exhibits, like the deep-sea fish and the fossils, are replicas, so they make calm, still subjects.
card.stand_here_before_gps_rule: Stand at the Cairns Aquarium itself, where the phone icon on the map sits. Once you're inside, get right up close to the glass of the big tanks and face the water.

card.hook: Picture this: the sun's gone, the stalls switch on, and suddenly a whole lane of souvenir tables is glowing like a fairground. That's the Cairns Night Markets, and the evening buzz is the real star.
card.stand_here: Stand right at the phone icon on the map, inside Cairns Night Markets along the stall lanes. There's no outdoor spot for the outside of the market, so walk the lanes slowly and face down a lane of lit stalls.
card.zoom: Start at zoom 1x for stalls and the lit food court. Switch to zoom 0.5x in the wider lanes to fit in rows of stalls and the crowd. Try zoom 2x or more (depends on your phone) for details on souvenir tables.
card.make_it_pop: Tap a lit stall, then slide the brightness down a little so the bright lights don't wash out.
card.best_time: Come in the evening after dark, once the lights are on. One guide also says golden hour just before sunset is a pleasant time to arrive.
card.selfie_here: Hold your phone at arm's length, use the front camera, and tuck a glowing row of stalls behind your shoulder. If your phone has a 0.5x front option, it'll fit more of the lights in.
card.rules_and_safety: Photos for personal use are generally fine. Be polite to stallholders, and ask permission before taking close-up photos of people.
card.challenge: Find the most colourful souvenir display in the market, put it in the foreground, and let the crowd blur into the background behind it.
card.good_to_know: The market is fully undercover, so it's a good plan in rain or sun. There are entrances at 73-75 Esplanade and on Abbott Street, so you can loop through from one to the other. Entry is described as free, but check the official site for opening times before you go.
card.stand_here_before_gps_rule: Stand right at the phone icon on the map, inside Cairns Night Markets along the stall lanes. There's no outdoor spot for the outside of the market, so walk the lanes slowly and face down a lane of lit stalls.

selfie_research.notes: No page I found names a selfie spot with the Cairns Night Markets behind the visitor, or a spot where a passer-by should stand to photograph a visitor with the whole market in frame. The results were reviews, photo-gallery pages and visitor guides that describe the market in general. The only location details are the two entrances: one on Abbott Street and one on the Esplanade, with tripAtrek noting the Esplanade entrance sits opposite Cairns Lagoon (tripatrek.com, shopping-and-food guide). Those are entrances, not photo spots, so I have not listed them. Sources also disagree on the address: planetwhitley.com gives 54-60 Abbott Street as correct and says 71-75 Esplanade is outdated, while Tripadvisor and Yelp still list 71/73-75 Esplanade. No page states any selfie-stick or tripod rule for this market. The only photography guidance I found is from airial.travel: personal photography is generally allowed, and visitors should ask permission before taking close-up photos of individuals. That is a general photography rule, not a selfie-stick or tripod rule, so I have left it out of 'rules'. The safety point I could have taken from airial.travel concerns glass-blowing demonstrations, not selfies, so I have left 'safety' blank. Checking the market on site would be the only way to find a real spot.

card.hook: Cairns has a garden where the plants get a second showing upside down in the water. Come at the right moment and the lake does half the work for you.
card.stand_here: Stand at the edge of Centenary Lakes, near the Chinese friendship garden. Face out across the water so the lake and the garden plants are in front of you, reflections and all. The main garden and its lawn are behind you to the north-west.
card.zoom: Start at 1x, which keeps the water and plants looking natural. Go to 0.5x to fit in more of the lake edge, or 2x to pick out one plant and its reflection.
card.make_it_pop: Turn on the gridlines and put the water's edge on the lower third line, so the reflections fill the frame and the horizon stays level.
card.best_time: Go around sunset, when the lake reflections are at their best. Wait for the water to calm down before you shoot, and check the official site for opening hours first if you're planning a late visit.
card.selfie_here: Walk to the lakeside near the Chinese Friendship Garden, ideally around sunset, and turn your back to the water. Use the front camera (or 0.5x if you want more of the scene) and let the reflections glow behind you. Another option is the bridge where the path follows Saltwater Creek towards the picnic and playground area, with the creek and rainforest greenery behind you.
card.ask_someone: Hand your phone to a passer-by and stand on the approach in front of the Visitor Information Centre, near the Flecker Garden entrance, with your back to the building so its reflective exterior is behind you.
card.challenge: Take one shot where the reflection looks so good that a friend has to ask which way up it is.
card.good_to_know: Cairns Botanic Gardens, once known as Flecker Botanical Gardens, began in the mid-1880s as part of a recreation reserve, only about ten years after Cairns was first surveyed. It became a permanent recreation reserve of about 44 hectares in 1921 and joined the Queensland Heritage Register in 2007. Centenary Lakes is a separate section reached by a boardwalk across Collins Avenue, so give yourself extra time.
card.stand_here_before_gps_rule: Stand at the edge of Centenary Lakes, near the Chinese friendship garden. Face out across the water so the lake and the garden plants are in front of you, reflections and all. The main garden and its lawn are behind you to the north-west.

selfie_spots.why: Small ornate bridges over the gardens' waterways are described as picture-perfect, and this one puts the creek and rainforest greenery behind you.

selfie_research.notes: The visitor centre is a building inside the gardens, not the whole landmark, so the passer-by spot only shows part of the site; no page named a spot that frames the whole gardens. Most sources are blogs, photo sites and aggregators rather than official tourism pages, except the Cairns Regional Council page, which only supports the visitor centre as a photo focus. The bridge spot names no bridge, only the path and the picnic area it leads to. A blogger mentioned mosquito bites at the lake at sunset, but no page gave a safety warning, so safety is blank.

card.hook: Plot twist: Cairns railway station is tucked into a shopping centre, with the platforms under the car park. It's a working station, not a postcard, and that's the charm.
card.stand_here: Stand on the Bunda Street footpath outside Cairns railway station, where you've got a clear view of the whole frontage. The phone icon on the map marks the spot. Face the entrance and step back until the whole thing fits.
card.zoom: Start at zoom 1x for a natural view. If the footpath is too narrow to step back, tap 0.5x to squeeze the whole entrance in. Use zoom 2x to 5x (depending on your phone) for signs and little details.
card.make_it_pop: Turn on the gridlines and line the building up with them so the vertical lines stay straight, then tap the building so it doesn't go too dark against a bright sky.
card.best_time: Morning or late afternoon gives softer light on the frontage. Quiet moments between train departures make it easier to get a clear view.
card.selfie_here: Flip to the front camera, tap 0.5x, and hold the phone a little higher so the station entrance sits behind your shoulder. Take a few, because people keep walking through.
card.rules_and_safety: The frontage is on a public footpath, but the platforms and trains are part of a working station and ticketed tourist railways, so check the official site before you go.
card.challenge: Take one wide shot and one closer shot of the entrance, and wait for a passing group to walk through for a bit of street life.
card.good_to_know: The first station here opened in 1891 as a two-storey timber building with ornate verandahs. It was replaced in 1955 by a cream brick building, and today's station opened on 7 May 1996 on the opposite side of the site. So don't go looking for Victorian verandahs, because this one is modern.
card.stand_here_before_gps_rule: Stand on the Bunda Street footpath outside Cairns railway station, where you've got a clear view of the whole frontage. The phone icon on the map marks the spot. Face the entrance and step back until the whole thing fits.

selfie_research.notes: No page I found names a selfie spot with Cairns railway station behind the visitor, so I have returned no selfie spots rather than guess. The station is described as tucked behind the Cairns Central shopping centre and not visible from the main street (note.com blog, https://note.com/hirotakahiro2/n/n9aaaf269a9b2?hl=en). It can be reached from Bunda Street or Spence Street (Kuranda Train & Skyrail, https://www.kuranda.tours/?ims=Kuranda&kw=kuranda). The only station-view photo spot mentioned is 'Cairns Station seen from the railroad crossing next to the station' on the same note.com page. That crossing is not named on any page, so I could not give it as a findable ask-someone spot; ask_someone_spot is null. The Barron Falls stop and the Stoney Creek Bridge are photo spots on the Kuranda train route, not at the station, so I excluded them. No page gave selfie stick or tripod rules for this area, and the only safety advice I found (stay behind barriers) is for the Barron Falls photo stop, not the station. Search coverage was limited, so a local travel guide or a visit may turn up a station-front spot.

card.hook: Back in 1928, this corner was the big new thing in Cairns. It was one of the largest buildings in town and one of only two with three storeys, and it still has the confident look to match.
card.stand_here: Stand on the pavement at the corner of Lake Street and Shields Street, facing the hotel's corner. Step back as far as the pavement allows so the whole building fits in.
card.zoom: Start at zoom 0.5x to fit the whole corner and both verandahs. Switch to 1x for a more natural look with less stretching at the edges. Then try 2x or more (depending on your phone) for the HIDES CAIRNS HOTEL lettering and the flagpole.
card.make_it_pop: Turn on your gridlines and line up the corner of the building with a vertical line so the walls don't lean.
card.best_time: Mornings or late afternoons usually give softer light on the walls than the middle of the day. Wait a moment for a gap in the people and traffic crossing the bottom of your shot.
card.selfie_here: Use the front camera from the pavement, switch to 0.5x, and tuck the hotel's corner and verandahs in behind your shoulder. Hold the phone a bit higher so the lettering along the top doesn't get cut off.
card.rules_and_safety: Shields Street near the hotel is a pedestrian mall, so check for street works or events before you go. You can photograph the outside from the public street.
card.challenge: Get the verandahs, the lettering and the corner all in one frame, with no strangers walking across the bottom. Patience is the secret ingredient.
card.good_to_know: Cairns architect Sydenham Stanley Oxenham designed the hotel. It was built in 1928 in reinforced concrete, and the Shields Street side was finished by about 1936. It joined the Queensland Heritage Register in 1992. An earlier timber Hides' Cairns Hotel from 1885, with double verandahs and an observation tower, stood beside this site, though it's long gone.
card.stand_here_before_gps_rule: Stand on the pavement at the corner of Lake Street and Shields Street, facing the hotel's corner. Step back as far as the pavement allows so the whole building fits in.

selfie_research.notes: No page I found names a selfie spot or a passer-by photo position for Hides Hotel (87 Lake Street, Cairns). The results were hotel booking pages, Tripadvisor traveller photo captions, a heritage listing, and general Cairns heritage guides. The only location-type detail is that the hotel sits on the south-west corner of Shields and Lake Streets (Queensland heritage listing, Cairns City Council draft schedule). That describes the site, not a photo position, so I did not list it as a spot. A Tripadvisor caption mentions a 'balcony where everyone hung out' and another mentions a breakfast verandah overlooking City Mall; these are traveller photo captions, not selfie guidance, so I excluded them. No page gave selfie stick or tripod rules, and none gave a safety point for this site. Suggested next step: check a current Cairns photo-spot guide or local tourism page before relying on any specific position.

card.hook: Conferences, concerts and Taipans basketball all happen behind one front door, and that front door is the bit you'll want in your photo. Good news: it's easy to find.
card.stand_here: Stand on Wharf Street, right across from the main entrance, so the centre is to the west of you and you're looking at the entrance and facade straight on.
card.zoom: Start at zoom 1x for a natural straight-on shot of the entrance. If the whole facade won't fit from the pavement, tap 0.5x, and use 2x for signs and architectural details.
card.make_it_pop: Turn on your gridlines and line the building's horizontal edges up with them so the facade doesn't lean (at 0.5x, don't tilt the phone upwards, because it stretches the edges).
card.best_time: Go when the sun isn't directly behind the entrance, which is often early morning or late afternoon, but check where the light falls when you arrive. Between events it's quieter, so you'll get a clearer view.
card.selfie_here: Try the outdoor Trinity Terrace on the top level: face out over Trinity Inlet with the building behind you, use the front camera, and switch to 0.5x to fit more in. It's a function venue, so check on arrival whether you can get up there.
card.ask_someone: Ask a passer-by to stand on the Wharf Street footpath near the corner with Sheridan Street, shooting along the coloured sun blades of the facade so the whole centre fits, while you pose in front of the building.
card.rules_and_safety: Keep to the pavement and watch for traffic and people arriving for events. You can photograph the frontage from the public street, but entry to the venue depends on events, so check the official site first.
card.challenge: Take your straight-on shot with the entrance dead centre and the roof edge perfectly level on the gridlines. Bonus points if a stranger walks through and gives it some scale.
card.good_to_know: The centre covers about 31,000 square metres on a 2.2-hectare site in the city centre. Stage one opened on 26 June 1996, and it was described as Australia's first regional convention centre and the country's first environmentally designed public building. An expansion adding meeting space and a third level was planned, so it may look different from older photos.
card.stand_here_before_gps_rule: Stand on Wharf Street, right across from the main entrance, so the centre is to the west of you and you're looking at the entrance and facade straight on.

selfie_spots.name: Trinity Terrace (top level, Cairns Convention Centre)
selfie_spots.detail: on the outdoor Trinity Terrace on the top level, facing out over Trinity Inlet with the building behind

selfie_research.notes: Only one selfie spot is supported by a page. The Trinity Terrace is a function venue. Its public access and whether the building sits behind a visitor facing the inlet are not confirmed by any page, so check on arrival. Wharf Street is named as the viewpoint of a photo of the centre, but no page names an exact spot on the footpath. The Esplanade Lagoon pages describe sunrise and sunset photos of the lagoon, not the convention centre, so I left them out. A Wikimedia Commons photo of the centre gives a camera position close to the given coordinates, facing south, but it is not a named place, so I did not use it. No page gives rules on selfie sticks or tripods, and no page gives a safety point for this landmark.

card.hook: Most street corners give you one era of history. This one gives you at least three: an old verandahed section, a fancy parapet and a later Art Deco stretch, all in a single frame.
card.stand_here: Stand at the south-western corner of Lake Street and Shields Street, outside the Cairns School of Arts. Face the building's main corner so the junction frames it for you.
card.zoom: Start at 1x for the whole corner facade. If pavement or traffic stops you stepping back, switch to 0.5x. Then try 2x or higher for close-ups of the parapet and the lettering.
card.make_it_pop: Turn on the gridlines, hold your phone upright to fit both storeys, and line the building's vertical edges up with the lines.
card.best_time: Check on site, because the front can be shaded or busy with pedestrians at some times. Traffic and people pass the corner, so wait for a gap and take a few frames.
card.selfie_here: Use the front camera at 0.5x, and stand so the building's corner and verandahs sit behind your shoulder. Hold your phone a little low and tilt up to catch both storeys.
card.rules_and_safety: You can photograph the outside from the public street. The building is a working museum, so check the official Cairns Museum site before you go if you want to go inside.
card.challenge: Get the date and the School of Arts lettering in one shot with the walls dead straight, then grab a 2x close-up of your favourite detail.
card.good_to_know: The School of Arts opened on 5 December 1907 and was designed by Tunbridge, Tunbridge & Lynch. It was an early use of reinforced concrete in Queensland. Later extensions ran along Lake Street, and the last one, in 1939-40, was Art Deco. Today it houses the Cairns Museum, run by the Cairns Historical Society.
card.stand_here_before_gps_rule: Stand at the south-western corner of Lake Street and Shields Street, outside the Cairns School of Arts. Face the building's main corner so the junction frames it for you.

selfie_research.notes: No page I found names a selfie spot with the Cairns School of Arts behind the visitor, or a passer-by spot for a photo of the visitor with the whole building. I did not add any place from memory, so both lists are empty. Coordinates match the heritage register entry for the building at the south-western corner of Lake and Shields streets, 93-105 Lake Street (https://apps.des.qld.gov.au/heritage-register/detail/?id=600380). Possible on-site features named by pages, but not described as photo spots: an inscribed terrazzo slab reading SCHOOL OF ARTS in the footpath at the building's corner (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cairns_School_of_Arts), and the timber verandahs on both street frontages (same heritage register page). No page I found gives selfie-stick or tripod rules, or a safety point for this site. The search was limited to one or two queries per step, so a further search for Cairns City Place or Shields Street Mall photo guides might find a named spot.

card.hook: Cairns has only one cathedral, and its front door opens straight onto Abbott Street. That means you can stand across the road and get the whole front looking proudly square-on.
card.stand_here: Stand on Abbott Street, directly opposite the main entrance of St Monica's Cathedral. Face the cathedral so the front facade is right in front of you.
card.zoom: Start at zoom 1x for a natural view of the front. If the whole facade won't fit from across the street, tap zoom 0.5x, which also squeezes in some of the gardens and neighbouring church buildings. Zoom 2x is handy for the doorway and details.
card.make_it_pop: Switch on the gridlines, put the main door on the centre line, and hold your phone upright and level so the walls don't lean.
card.best_time: Early morning or late afternoon usually gives softer light on the front of the building than the middle of the day. Your pale walls and sky will thank you.
card.selfie_here: Try the imposing front stairs on the Minnie Street side of the cathedral, which make a likely backdrop. The gardens around the building are another pretty spot. Use the front camera at 0.5x and keep the cathedral over your shoulder.
card.rules_and_safety: This is a working church, so respect services and worshippers. Inside, keep the flash off, keep your distance from anyone praying, and stick to the public areas. Only take photos of the stained-glass windows if photography is allowed when you visit.
card.challenge: Get the door dead centre on the gridline with straight, upright walls. Bonus points if nobody's thumb sneaks into the corner.
card.good_to_know: St Monica's was designed by Brisbane architect Ian Ferrier and built in 1967–68 as a war memorial dedicated to the Battle of the Coral Sea. It has been on the Queensland Heritage Register since 31 August 1998. Ferrier also designed the cathedrals in Darwin and Port Moresby.
card.stand_here_before_gps_rule: Stand on Abbott Street, directly opposite the main entrance of St Monica's Cathedral. Face the cathedral so the front facade is right in front of you.

selfie_research.notes: No page I found names a specific outdoor selfie spot or a named place where a passer-by should stand to photograph a visitor with the whole cathedral; the first spot is inferred from the stairs' description, and the second is a general garden area. A Wikimedia photo was taken from a Holiday Inn seventh-floor room on Florence Street, which is not a public spot, so I excluded it. Photography guides say photography is generally permitted, with no flash and no walking onto the pulpit, but they say nothing about selfie sticks or tripods, so no rule about those is reported. Sources give the address as both 181 and 183 Abbott Street.

card.hook: There's a pale, tidy little 1930s building parked right in front of a casino hotel, and it looks like it has no idea it's surrounded. Its symmetry makes it easy to photograph.
card.stand_here: Stand on Abbott Street, in front of the Abbott Street entrance and across the road from the portico. From here the building lies to the north-east, so face that way and you'll see the whole classical front.
card.zoom: Start at zoom 1x to fit the whole facade in. If traffic or the kerb stops you stepping back, switch to zoom 0.5x, but don't use it up close because it stretches and tilts the building. Then try zoom 2x or more for the parapet and pilasters.
card.make_it_pop: Turn on gridlines and line up the pilasters with the vertical lines so the building doesn't lean.
card.best_time: Early morning or late afternoon usually gives softer light on the pale walls than the middle of the day. Quieter times at the entrance make it easier to get a clear shot.
card.selfie_here: Turn your back to the building, use the front camera, and tilt the phone up a little so the portico sits over your shoulder. If your phone has zoom 0.5x on the front camera, it will help squeeze more of the building in.
card.rules_and_safety: You can photograph the front from the street. If you want to go inside, check the official site first, as it's a restaurant.
card.challenge: Get one shot where the pilasters are dead straight on the gridlines and nobody is walking through the doorway.
card.good_to_know: Architect Robert Henry Bowen designed it, and it was built in 1936-37 as a Depression-era project to create jobs. It was the third customs house on this site, which has been tied to the port of Cairns since the 1870s. Today it's a restaurant inside the Reef Hotel Casino complex.
card.stand_here_before_gps_rule: Stand on Abbott Street, in front of the Abbott Street entrance and across the road from the portico. From here the building lies to the north-east, so face that way and you'll see the whole classical front.

selfie_research.notes: No page I found names a selfie spot with Cairns Customs House behind the visitor, or a passer-by spot for photographing a visitor with the whole building. I have left both empty rather than guess. Pages found that describe the building: Wikipedia 'Cairns Customs House' (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cairns_Customs_House), which gives the address as 6A-8A Abbott Street and says the site has frontages to Abbott Street and the Esplanade; Aussie Towns 'Cairns, QLD' (https://www.aussietowns.com.au/town/cairns-qld), which describes the Abbott Street entrance facade with classical moulded details and a projecting entrance portico; and the Queensland Heritage Register entry (https://apps.des.qld.gov.au/heritage-register/explorer/detail/?id=600377). The Crystalbrook blog (https://www.crystalbrookcollection.com/blog-tnq) names Esplanade Boardwalk access via 68-72 Abbott Street, which is near the building, but does not say it is a photo spot for this landmark. Possible next step: check a local photo-spot guide or a Cairns Esplanade or Abbott Street walking guide for a named standpoint before adding a spot. No rules on selfie sticks or tripods and no safety point were found on any page.
